body:
CORRECTING MY OWN DEPRIORITISATION OF DNLT-BP. The owner asked whether we dismissed it for being
Portuguese. We did not, but I gave the wrong reason and I had the two costs backwards.

WHAT I SAID at 20:50: DNLT-BP is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with additional research/clinical language, so it
needs an owner decision "because the licence constrains what this LIBRARY may become, not just
what we may read."

THAT WAS TOO STRONG AND PARTLY WRONG. SHARE-ALIKE ON THE DATA DOES NOT INFECT OUR CODE. SA
attaches to derivatives OF THE DATA. Software that reads a corpus is not a derivative of it, and
if we do not redistribute the corpus or derivatives of it, storymodel4s carries no SA obligation
at all. I conflated "a licence on the data" with "a licence constraint on the project", and the
owner's fair-use ruling weakens what remains.

THE REAL BARRIER IS PORTUGUESE, AND I MEASURED IT INSTEAD OF ASSERTING IT:

  core/atlas.scala:14   LanguageTag.English exists, and at :114 it is a DEFAULT PARAMETER rather
                        than a hardcoded constant. Somebody designed for this.
  recall/lexical.scala  440+ lines of ENGLISH MORPHOLOGY -- stemming, irregular-form mapping,
                        final-y normalisation ("cry" vs "cri"), documented as "generic English".
  recall/segmenter.scala  hardcoded English clause connectives.

So a Portuguese path is A MODULE, NOT A FLAG. Not a fundamental barrier -- the architecture
anticipated multilingual work -- but real.

AND THE SEQUENCING ARGUMENT I SHOULD HAVE MADE INSTEAD OF THE LICENCE ONE: our provider currently
handles 4 OF 50 ENGLISH SENTENCES. Running it on Portuguese now means WE CANNOT DISTINGUISH
PROVIDER FAILURE FROM LANGUAGE FAILURE. That is a diagnostic problem, not a legal one, and it is
the actual reason to sequence DNLT-BP after the English path proves itself.

WHAT DNLT-BP HAS THAT NOTHING ELSE IN THE SURVEY HAS, and it is not a small thing: PAIRED
IMMEDIATE AND DELAYED RETELLINGS FROM THE SAME PARTICIPANT. That is a within-participant
longitudinal contrast -- Bartlett's REPEATED reproduction, where Ost gptkz gives us SERIAL
reproduction. Those are different phenomena and a library about story recall wants both. Plus a
clinical contrast (MCI, Alzheimer's, healthy older adults) that no other open corpus in the survey
offers.

REVISED POSITION: DNLT-BP is a WHEN, not a WHETHER. It is third in line behind NFRD and gptkz, on
diagnostic grounds rather than licence grounds, and the thing that unblocks it is a Portuguese
lexical module plus separately obtaining the Wallet source-story texts, which the repository does
not appear to contain.

Recorded because I gated a corpus on the wrong axis and the owner caught it.
